title: Record the scalar prime support of the selected PR6030 word
body: ## Change and mathematical scope Scoped census; no new κ. On the selected PR6030 word, every `ADD`, `SCALE` and `COPY` coefficient is a nonzero rational whose numerator and denominator, in lowest terms, are divisible only by the primes 2, 3, 5 and 7. Writing `q = σ · 2^v · m` with `m` positive and odd, - `m ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7, 9}`, - `v ∈ {-4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4}`. There are 19,288 such coefficients and 31 distinct values. `16q` is an integer for every one of them, and 16 is the least positive integer with that property. `|16q| ≤ 256`, attained at `q = -16` (three `ADD` events). The coefficient `+16` does not occur. Every `COPY` coefficient is `+1`. Assumption ID: `analytic_recovery`. This is the scalar-tape input of that assumption on this caller. It is not a proof of analytic decomposition, fine-prime avoidance for Gaussian entries or `MOVE` charts, or the outer framework. Selected conditional κ stays `781451/250000000`. The five framework assumptions remain. ## Task and overlap Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`. Priority revision 8. Catalogue card `uniform-transfer-audit`. Scope status: **refined**. Session r105 takes item 8 of the ordered eligible list. Open handoffs are dropped when the post is completed, a merged result answers the question, the canonical artifact is an open pull request, or the post says no target was taken. That removes the delivered 19 October index, the H25 chain, the 2 November review artifacts, and the PR6551 handoff. The 16:01 seven-call note updates the 15:36 note, so they are one request. No structured claim was unexpired at 2026-11-08T13:14:24Z. Work already delivered by this account is excluded. Three open handoffs remain, the revision-8 next-decision table then supplies six rows, and unnamed catalogue cards follow: 1. Three signed added frames at seven calls (discussion #1166 comment 19377832, updating 19377345). 2. Eight-source singleton connector at length 30 (comment 19377982). 3. Six-source depth-two block at `c = 7` (comment 19384981). 4. Complex helpers (`p104-side-correction`, `coverage-law-change`). 5. BIT (`bit-helper-contract`). 6. New decoders and interfaces. 7. Supplier audit (`supplier-boundary-audit`). 8. **This package.** All-size audit (`uniform-transfer-audit`): scalar prime support of `analytic_recovery`. 9. Verification tooling (`replay-runtime`). 10. `bit-new-register-model`. Inside this row, #5837, #6293, #6522 and #6635 are different implications. The live input is `research/p104-helper470-twin-rung-removal/WORD.json.gz` (SHA256 `7834725d9e34ee846a9ccc615221ea81e0201613938afa185d2eda0c9a6c232f`). Nearest work: - unpaidmoon #6635, `research/pr6030-scalar-chart-lift`: the same coefficients factor out of the tensor power. It does not classify them. - unpaidmoon #6293: `MOVE` phase `i^{p f}`. - unpaidmoon #6522: the coordinate-envelope exponent `2^(10^9+240152f)`. - unpaidmoon #5837: the scalar lift on the older #5599 word. - Ali Romman #6513: tape routes for width-64 scalar templates, not these factorizations. Open-PR titles and bodies on 2026-11-08 did not state this census. The discussion snapshot covered all 3,528 comments on #1166. This fork draft is based on `cursor/upstream-7c49fe32-pin-2868` because the fork's `main` is 3,973 commits behind that pin. The scientific base is upstream `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`. ## Validation CPython 3.12.3, standard library, Linux. From the repository root: ```sh python3 -B research/pr6030-scalar-prime-support/verify.py python3 -O -B research/pr6030-scalar-prime-support/verify.py python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pr6030-scalar-prime-support python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/pr6030-scalar-prime-support --check-source-history python3 -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py ``` Observed: `PASS_PR6030_SCALAR_PRIME_SUPPORT` with `events=19288 distinct=31 adds=18404 scales=861 copies=23 denom_lcm=16 max_abs_16q=256 odd_primes=3,5,7 valuation=-4..4 no_new_kappa=true`, the same marker under `-O`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with outcome `partial`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`. The baseline command is not a supplier replay. Failure controls reject `0`, `11`, `1/3`, `1/32`, `32`, `15`, `27` and `1/48`. Not run: `make frontier6030-verify`, the primary native replay, Lean, Gaussian or `MOVE` factorization, and an outer analytic-recovery proof. All five selected framework assumptions remain. ## Credit Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. The selected word is DreamingOfClouds' PR #6030. The selected review is `docs/research/pr-intake-evidence/pr6030-audit/PROOF-REVIEW.md`. Predecessor scalar and phase notes: unpaidmoon #5837, #6293, #6522 and #6635. Those files are not modified. ## Open next questions 1. Do the non-scalar payloads of this word, including Gaussian integer entries and `MOVE` chart matrices, stay inside the primes `{2, 3, 5, 7}`? First step: factor one rank-r Gaussian row from the primary native payload. Blocked because that payload is not an input here. 2. Does the retained analytic-recovery modulus already allow denominator 16 and odd primes `{3, 5, 7}`, or does the outer framework demand a larger avoided-prime set? First step: compare this support with the retained fine-prime padding bound. Blocked because this note does not vendor that argument, and the census does not discharge `analytic_recovery`. ## Workflow feedback (optional) The revision-8 table still names the older #5599 exponent in its opening paragraph, while `certificates/selected-result.json` selects PR6030 at `781451/250000000`. Reading the selected record before the priority prose avoided classifying the stale word. A link to discussion #1200 is enough.
